name: Jelqing

lead: Jelqing is a manual technique in which a man strokes or squeezes a semi-erect penis from base toward the head, aiming to increase length or girth. It circulates in looksmaxxing forums under labels such as girthmaxxing and lengthmaxxing, and many people report personal gains online.

Proponents describe the chain as repeated stretching that causes microscopic tears in erectile tissue which heal larger. Some forum members counter that stretching only enlarges existing chambers and lowers tissue density. Wikipedia states that medical evidence for the technique is absent, and no clinical study of jelqing's effect was found.

paras: Practitioners do short daily sessions with lubrication, often alongside stretching, pumps or other enlargement methods, and report tracking measurements over months.

Clinicians cited by Wikipedia caution against routine or aggressive jelqing because of possible fibrosis and plaque formation, and it may raise the risk of hard flaccid syndrome. Penis size anxiety, which often motivates the practice, has been studied separately as a body dysmorphic concern.

social.title: Jelqing: The latest in a long history of attempts to enlarge the male member

angle.text: Practitioners stroke and stretch the penis in the belief that tissue remodels and grows larger over time. Many people report gains online, but no clinical study has measured an enlargement effect.

lead: Jelqing is a manual technique that people use in the hope of making the penis longer or thicker. It is done on the semi-erect penis, with the hand moving from base toward the head in a repeated stroking or squeezing motion. Wikipedia lists it, alongside pumps and traction devices, among the non-surgical physical methods of penis enlargement. [1][2]

Users pursue it for the same reason as other enlargement methods: a larger-looking or larger-feeling body part can improve how a man feels about his appearance. Looksmaxxing forums discuss it under labels such as girthmaxxing and lengthmaxxing, and some members report gains from it while others dispute that any gain lasts. [3][4]

Wikipedia states that medical evidence for the technique is absent, that many people nevertheless report success, and that clinicians caution against routine or aggressive manipulation. [1] The word is said to derive from the Persian jalq zadan, and the practice is attributed to ancient Arab origins. [1]
infobox: Fibrosis, plaque formation, hard flaccid syndrome [1]

paras: Jelqing is performed on the semi-erect penis by moving the hand from base to head with a combined squeezing and stroking motion; it is also called milking. [1] Forum discussions describe it as one of several physical enlargement routes alongside stretchers and pumps. [3]

Wikipedia places it among the physical techniques, which also include vacuum pumping and traction. It notes that traction is the only physical method for which limited scientific evidence of some elongation exists, with studies of traction mostly in men with Peyronie's disease, and that evidence of lengthening from traction in other men is mixed. [1] Wikipedia describes supplements and ointments sold for enlargement as generally considered ineffective, and surgical methods as carrying significant risk; the American Urological Association has stated that fat injection and ligament division for enlargement have not been shown to be safe or efficacious. [1]

A looksmax.org post argues that jelqing and other physical enlargement methods work by stretching erectile tissue to cause microtears that heal to increase volume. The same post argues that this enlarges existing erectile chambers rather than adding new ones, which it says would lower erectile tissue density, and applies the same reasoning to the Bathmate pump. [3] These are forum claims; no clinical study has tested the mechanism.

Clinicians cited by Wikipedia caution against routine use, particularly excessive or aggressive manipulation, because of possible fibrosis and plaque formation, and say it may increase the risk of hard flaccid syndrome. [1]

Wikipedia also notes that some doctors say most men seeking enlargement have normal-sized penises and may underestimate their own size while overestimating the average, a pattern described as penile dysmorphophobia. [1]

Threads on looksmax.org range from routines and progress reports to warnings. One member plans morning sessions and asks how long to continue and whether to add clamping; replies disagree on whether the practice has permanent effect. [4] Another thread titled as a warning argues jelqing leaves erectile tissue of lower density. [3]
On T Nation, jelqing has long been a running joke in banter threads, and one 2023 poster in a different thread says daily jelqing and a pump helped with sensitivity. [5][6]

Hacker News carried a 2026 link to an article titled 'Jelqing: The latest in a long history of attempts to enlarge the male member', indicating mainstream-press interest in the practice's recent popularity. [7]

No studies found testing jelqing. A 2015 cohort study of 90 men compared men with body dysmorphic disorder concerning penis size, men with small penis anxiety, and controls. It found that men with either concern were more likely than controls to have tried to change penis size or shape, for example by jelqing, vacuum pumps or stretching devices, and reported reduced sexual-function measures in the dysmorphic group. It did not test whether jelqing changes size. [8]

lore.intro: On looksmax.org, jelqing is discussed both as a size-increase method and as a practice some members warn against, with members disagreeing about whether any gain is permanent. [3][4]

claims.claim: Jelqing stretches erectile tissue, causing microtears that heal into a larger penis.
Jelqing and similar methods enlarge the existing erectile chambers without adding new ones, lowering erectile tissue density.
Any gain from jelqing is only temporary.
